html:
Track-On2 and Track-On-R (Aydemir et al., 2025): online point tracking, one frame at a time, as a transformer decoder over a DINOv3 ViT-S+ adapter with a memory of past features; -R is fine-tuned on real videos. MIT; DINOv3 weights under the DINOv3 License.

Details
  • Paper: Track-On2: Enhancing Online Point Tracking with Memory, TPAMI 2026, 2025-09-23
  • Original code: https://github.com/gorkaydemir/track_on at 04efe8a137bd
  • Code licence: MIT AND LicenseRef-DINOv3-License (permissive); files: LICENSE, LICENSE.md
  • Weights licence: MIT AND LicenseRef-DINOv3-License
  • Licence evidence: https://huggingface.co/gorkaydemir/track_on2/blob/672a47c4614f6d661edc36b7999a5bb5c3a5d2c9/README.md (license: mit); https://huggingface.co/gorkaydemir/track_on_r/blob/9401fe5c9ec6e21fb4f6070f05ac9ce75e3c9845/README.md (license: mit); https://github.com/gorkaydemir/track_on/blob/04efe8a137bd76e45e07382f02748794c9b61a96/LICENSE (MIT)
  • Training data: Upstream README / paper: Track-On2 trained on Kubric MOVi-F (synthetic, 64-frame clips); Track-On-R fine-tuned on real-world videos with pseudo-labels from an ensemble of trackers (verifier). Neither has a dataset entry here yet. The frozen DINOv3 ViT-S+/16 was pretrained on LVD-1689M (not released).
  • Licence note: The DINOv3 ViT-S+/16 weights and net/dinov3.py are under the DINOv3 License (Meta: attribution and conditions apply); read it before commercial use. The Track-On code and checkpoints are MIT.
  • Options: memory = 72 (>= 1), support_grid = 20 (>= 0)
  • Kernel libraries: fastbb, dpt_fused
  • Variants: track-on2, track-on-r
  • Outputs: tracks, visibility
  • Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): track-on2 3000x4000 (5.0 GiB peak allocated, 6.0 reserved); track-on-r 3000x4000 (5.0 GiB peak allocated, 6.0 reserved)
  • track-on2 original 480x854: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); gorkaydemir/track_on@04efe8a137bd Predictor loop, 384 x 512, memory 72
  • track-on-r original 480x854: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); gorkaydemir/track_on@04efe8a137bd Predictor loop, 384 x 512, memory 72
  • track-on2 load / first call: original 3.77 s / 3.626 s, portable 0.46 s / 2.637 s, kernels 1.17 s / 1.753 s
  • track-on-r load / first call: original 0.88 s / 2.907 s, portable 0.24 s / 1.989 s, kernels 1.11 s / 1.72 s
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

TAP-Vid protocol: frames resized to 256 x 256 (PIL Lanczos) before the model (AllTracker: the original frames, resized by the model), one query per track at its first visible point, tracked online (TAPNext, Track-On) or over the whole clip (TAPIR, AllTracker, LocoTrack); AJ, delta_avg (< 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 px at 256 x 256) and occlusion accuracy averaged over the videos. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1.8e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.05 and p99 <= 1.2 (absolute error of the output tracks).

Limitations

  • Frames are resized to 384 x 512 (the size the learned position embedding was trained at), whatever their size and aspect ratio.
  • Upstream adds a 20 x 20 grid of support points on frame 0 to every call (option support_grid); they are tracked with the user's queries, so a call costs at least 400 tracked points.
  • Online: a query only sees the frames from its own frame on; frames before it return the query position with visibility 0.
  • One video per call; all queries of a call share the video.
